endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: For clarity, Customer Data shall be treated as Confidential Information under this Agreement, provided, however, that to the extent Customer Data constitutes PHI, such PHI shall be subject to the BAA.

endorsements.title: Utah HB 452 (2025), mental health chatbots
endorsements.quote: When sharing information under Subsection (3)(a), the supplier and the other entity shall comply with all applicable privacy and security provisions of 45 C.F.R. Part 160 and 45 C.F.R. Part 164

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: If protected health information (PHI) is involved, organizations should execute appropriate Business Associate Agreements, apply the “minimum necessary” standard, and maintain safeguards commensurate with risk.

endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: Appropriate governance policies should be developed by health care organizations and account for and mitigate risks of: i) Incorrect or falsified responses; lack of ability to readily verify the accuracy of responses or the sources used to generate the response.

endorsements.title: Bridging the gap: a practical step-by-step approach to warrant safe implementation of large language models in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Importantly, healthcare providers must be aware that they should establish strict contractual agreements with third-party LLM hosts to prevent data retention and ensure that user or patient data is not utilized for model retraining.

endorsements.title: Building a Safe and Transparent Workflow for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Clinical Trials and Prediction Models: A Technical Report
endorsements.quote: Keep protected/identifiable information off public tools; prefer institution-approved solutions under the right agreements (e.g., data processing agreement (DPA)/business associate agreement (BAA); document the legal basis (e.g., GDPR) and any required approvals; and align with local institutional policy [ 1 , 20 ].

endorsements.title: Expert Consensus Best Practices for the Safe, Ethical, and Effective Design and Implementation of Artificially Intelligent Conversational Agent (i.e., Chatbot/Virtual Human) Systems in Health Care Applications
endorsements.quote: When the LLM desired is not available through that format, a business associate agreement with a technology provider that can offer HIPAA and HITRUST compliance certifications and provide assurances that the data transmitted to their server is not available to anyone else, and the data are not used in any other way other than the agreed intended purpose.

endorsements.title: A practical guide to the implementation of AI in orthopaedic research-Part 4: Prerequisites for a successful orthopedics AI-driven project in terms of interdisciplinary collaboration, data management, ethical approval and technology
endorsements.quote: Vendors providing AI tools for clinical use must supply written documentation on: data retention schedules; incident response procedures; audit log architecture; and compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule's technical safeguards.

endorsements.title: Multimodal generative AI for pre-practicum mental health support competency development: a human-supervised framework for education-childcare partnerships
endorsements.quote: Vendor agreements cover documentation, data handling, subprocessors, security, limitations, material-change and breach notification, audit cooperation, and secure exit.

commentary.bottom_line: Nine sources endorse executing Business Associate Agreements before AI vendors handle PHI, including one state statute and one framework at the must level, but no study tests whether these agreements, or AI-specific terms within them, reduce improper PHI handling. The recommendation rests on legal obligation and expert consensus rather than measured outcomes.

perspectives.view: No study tests the practice, and no study documents the hazard's frequency or consequences. The nine endorsements include one statute, one framework, two guidance documents, and five commentaries. Under GRADE conventions, consensus statements do not substitute for tests of an intervention, so certainty about effect on PHI exposure cannot be rated.

Utah HB 452 requires mental health chatbot suppliers sharing information to comply with 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164. The CHAI playbook language routes vendor-held PHI to the BAA. Several commentaries add terms beyond standard HIPAA templates, such as limits on data retention, model retraining, and subprocessors, which suggests standard agreements may leave AI-specific uses unaddressed.

The supplied record contains no study showing how often AI vendors process PHI without enforceable obligations or what harm follows. The endorsed contract terms, including breach notification, incident response, and audit cooperation, describe mechanisms that could detect disclosures, but no evidence shows whether they catch problems before patient data is exposed.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare PHI incidents, retention violations, and unauthorized secondary use, such as model retraining, among AI vendor deployments governed by standard BAAs, BAAs with AI-specific terms, and no agreement. Audits of whether vendors comply with contract terms in practice would also show whether the agreements change vendor behavior.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems with limited legal staff may face more difficulty negotiating AI-specific terms, but the supplied record contains no data on that question.
